reviewScope: Black Whale vessel, spatial, access, operational, structural and scale evidence only

pass1.method: Full-page visual sweep of all 19 ordered pages

pass2.method: Full-resolution verification of royal-suite interiors, corridor thresholds, repeated doors, guard posts, communications hardware and temporary room-use states

retainedPanels.subject: Royal suite emergency interior
retainedPanels.visualDescription: The royal room remains a broad finished interior with multiple occupants separated across open floor, wall panels, furniture and a visible doorway zone.
modelingPermissions: Preserve a large occupiable royal-room class with broad circulation
modelingProhibitions: Do not infer exact dimensions or a complete suite plan

retainedPanels.subject: Royal corridor threshold
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A guard stands at a tall dark-paneled doorway opening onto the decorated royal corridor.
modelingProhibitions: Do not identify the room number without visible signage

retainedPanels.subject: Repeated royal corridor fronts
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A long finished corridor shows repeated tall room fronts, wall trim and enough width for guards and attendants to stand and pass in groups.
modelingPermissions: Extend the repeated-suite-front corridor system and broad circulation class
modelingProhibitions: Do not derive exact bay spacing or unseen room count

retainedPanels.subject: Royal suite meeting area
retainedPanels.visualDescription: A large table and several chairs occupy a formally decorated room while multiple people remain around its perimeter.
modelingPermissions: Permit a large furnished meeting zone within the shown royal room
modelingProhibitions: Do not treat furniture placement as immutable geometry

evidence.claim: The royal room supports several separated occupants, furniture and unobstructed movement within one enclosed finished interior.
The suite includes substantial fixed-looking wall treatment and large furniture while retaining circulation space.
evidence.modelingUse: Royal-suite finish and furnishing density class.

evidence.claim: A tall paneled doorway connects the occupied room to an adjoining circulation zone.
evidence.modelingUse: Register at least one major room threshold.

evidence.claim: A guard can hold position directly at a royal-room doorway facing the corridor.
evidence.modelingUse: Store controlled access as a chapter-state overlay.

evidence.claim: The same formal room accommodates several standing participants without collapsing into a narrow passage.
Conversation occurs with a tall paneled doorway and finished wall field visible behind the occupants.
Remote calls are conducted from within the royal residential room while other occupants remain present.
evidence.modelingUse: Operational communications state, without assuming fixed hardware.

evidence.claim: A character sketches a simplified room-and-corridor relation for tactical explanation, but the drawing is not verified architectural geometry.
evidence.modelingUse: Store only as quarantined route reasoning, not production geometry.

evidence.claim: Occupants move from the furnished room toward the corridor through a visible threshold sequence.
evidence.modelingUse: Support room-to-corridor connectivity without fixing adjacency beyond the shown transition.

evidence.claim: The royal residential zone has a long decorated corridor with repeated tall room fronts and space for group movement.
Several guards and attendants can cluster near one doorway while leaving passable corridor area.
evidence.modelingUse: Broad corridor-width class and temporary guard concentration.

evidence.claim: A formal room contains a large central table, multiple chairs and standing occupants around the perimeter.
The occupied royal room remains enclosed by continuous decorated wall surfaces with a distinct doorway opening.
A wall-mounted clock-like display and active remote communication are depicted inside the residential environment.
evidence.modelingUse: Register a possible fixed timekeeping fixture; quarantine exact device identity.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Tactical room diagram on page 12
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: The in-story sketch may simplify or distort spatial relations and cannot be promoted to production geometry without independent panel confirmation.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Repeated corridor thresholds
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: Repeated doors establish a corridor type but not exact room count, bay spacing or numbered adjacency.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Wall device on page 18
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: The panel supports a mounted timekeeping or display fixture, but exact system identity and network connection remain unknown.

unresolvedQuestions: Which numbered suite is associated with the guarded doorway on page 8?
Does the page 12 sketch preserve real adjacency or only explain a tactical idea?
Is the page 18 wall device a clock, timer or broader ship display?

excludedMaterial.reason: Excluded material does not independently establish Black Whale geometry, route, access, operational infrastructure, scale or durable chapter-state evidence.
